claim: Global Accelerator assigns each accelerator a default DNS name that points to its static IP addresses; the DNS name is not configurable, and you can use your own custom domain name by setting up DNS records.
question: How do clients reach an accelerator by name?

values.display: Global Accelerator assigns each accelerator a default Domain
the DNS name that Global Accelerator generates

evidence.quote: Global Accelerator assigns each accelerator a default Domain Name System (DNS) name, similar to `a1234567890abcdef.awsglobalaccelerator.com`, that points to the static IP addresses that Global Accelerator assigns to you or that you choose from your own IP address range.
Be aware that the DNS name that Global Accelerator generates for you isn't configurable, and you can't create PTR records that point to your custom domain name.

claim: With one BYOIP range you assign one of your addresses to the accelerator and Global Accelerator assigns a second static IP address from an Amazon range; with two ranges you can assign one address from each, because each range is in a different network zone.
question: How many of your own IP addresses can one accelerator use per BYOIP range?

values.display: assign one IP address from your range
assigns each address range to a different network

evidence.quote: When you create an accelerator, you can assign one IP address from your range to it. Global Accelerator assigns you a second static IP address from an Amazon IP address range. If you bring two IP address ranges to AWS, you can assign one IP address from each range to your accelerator. This restriction is because Global Accelerator assigns each address range to a different network zone, for high availability.
